author: Tony Marrero
title: 2nd suspect arrested in fatal shooting at St. Petersburg Childs Park YMCA - NewsBreak
text:
By Tony Marrero ,
7 hours ago Police have arrested a second suspect in connection to the fatal shooting at the Childs Park YMCA in St. Petersburg on July 22. [ DIRK SHADD | Times ] Police have arrested a second suspect in connection to last week’s fatal shooting at the Childs Park YMCA in St. Petersburg, and an arrest report for the first suspect includes new details about the case.
Jeremiah Peterson, 18, of St. Petersburg turned himself in Tuesday and was arrested on a charge of murder while engaged in robbery, according to the St. Peterburg Police Department.
The bench warrant for Peterson was listed as sealed by the court Wednesday. But an arrest report for his co-defendant, 18-year-old My’Kiese Johnson, provides new details not previously released by police about the July 22 shooting.
Jeremiah Peterson, 18, of St. Petersburg is pictured in a Pinellas County booking photo after his arrest Tuesday on a charge of murder while engaged in a robbery in connection to a fatal shooting at the Childs Park YMCA in St. Petersburg on July 22. [ St. Petersburg Police Department ] Among the new information is the name of the 18-year-old victim in the case: Deondre Wright. Police have not released Wright’s name, citing Marsy’s Law.
According to Johnson’s arrest report, Wright arranged to meet Johnson and Peterson at the YMCA, 691 43rd St. S., to buy a gun. Wright and Peterson went into the bathroom while Johnson and a friend of Wright’s waited in the hallway.
Wright’s friend heard a commotion in the bathroom and Wright called out to his friend for help. The friend later told police that he heard Peterson scream, “Give it up!” followed by several gunshots, according to the report.
At the same time, Wright’s friend saw Johnson start to pull a black gun from his waistband, “but the friend of the victim was faster and pulled his firearm and shot (Johnson),” the report states.
Wright’s friend left the area and called police to report what happened. Johnson also left and was seen tossing a gun that responding patrol officers later found, according to the report.
Johnson went to his grandmother’s house and she took him to Orlando Health Bayfront Hospital in St. Petersburg to be treated for a gunshot wound to his nose. Police arrested him at the hospital.
My’Kiese Johnson, 18, is pictured in a Pinellas County booking photo released by the St. Petersburg Police Department after his arrest on Wednesday, July 22, 2026 on a murder charge. [ St. Petersburg Police Department ] Johnson identified himself on a screen shot from a city-owned surveillance camera that showed him arriving with Peterson to the YMCA, according to the report. Wright’s friend also reviewed the photo and confirmed that Johnson was the person he shot in the hallway.
Wright was taken to Orlando Health Bayfront with a gunshot wound to his torso and died there.
Johnson is also being charged with murder while engaged in a robbery, also known as felony murder. It’s a capital felony that carries a mandatory life sentence in prison or the death penalty.
In Florida, someone can be charged with felony murder if another person dies during the commission of certain crimes, such as kidnapping or robbery. Someone can be charged with felony murder in a fatal shooting case, for example, even if they didn’t pull the trigger.
Both Johnson and Peterson were being held without bond Wednesday in the Pinellas County Jail. Court records did not list defense attorneys for either as of Wednesday.
A screenshot of a GoFundMe campaign page to raise money for funeral expenses shows Deondre Wright, who was fatally shot at the Childs Park YMCA in St. Petersburg on July 22. [ gofundme.com ] A police spokesperson said Wednesday that investigators do not expect to charge anyone else in connection to the case.
Wright, who went by Dee, was a St. Petersburg native, according to his obituary.
“Always so respectful, never thought twice to lend a helping hand and always kept a beautiful smile on his face,“ his father LJ Wright wrote in a GoFundMe campaign to raise money for funeral expenses. ”He was truly a joy to be around. As the oldest of the bunch, all of his siblings on both sides of the family adored him and really looked up to him.”
